$comment: It ships LIVE AND EMPTY rather than absent, which is this unit's own provisional note: the
engagement has not been booked (OPEN-QUESTIONS Y13-pentest), and a register that did not exist
until there was something to put in it is a register nobody would build on the day they needed it.
AN EMPTY REGISTER IS NOT A CLEAN ONE. `engagement.booked` is false, and `pnpm go-live:security`
refuses while it is: 'no findings' and 'nobody looked' are the same register, which is ADR 0002's
shape applied to a security review. That is why the go-live check is NOT in `pnpm verify` — it
exits non-zero today and is supposed to, exactly as `pnpm go-live:payments` does.
What IS in `pnpm verify` is `pnpm findings`, which checks this file's integrity: closed severity and
status sets, and the closing rule — a finding cannot be fixed without a commit or a test reference,
accepted without a rationale and a role, dismissed as a false positive without a reason, or marked
a duplicate without naming the original.
There is deliberately no digest over this file. The restore drill's report has one (ADR 0123)
because it is a measurement and a hand edit to it is always a falsification; this is a working
document somebody edits on purpose, and its control is the closing rule plus the review of the diff.
To add findings from the stand-in scan: `pnpm security-scan --target <url> --import`.

engagement.standIn: an automated unauthenticated baseline scan over the route list the registry declares, exercised against a deliberately vulnerable fixture origin so that it is known to find what is there (scripts/security-baseline-scan.mjs)
